01 / Company decoded

SARVAM

Bengaluru-based full-stack sovereign AI company building across infrastructure, research and deployment—not just a model demo.

Main feature

AI, built
for India.

Founded in July 2023 by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam describes a full-stack approach to sovereign AI: training and inference infrastructure, frontier-model research, and go-to-market for enterprises, developers and government.

SOVEREIGN AI

The thesis

India needs AI systems designed around its languages, institutions, users and deployment realities. Sarvam combines models with the infrastructure and routes to market needed to put them into use.

July 2023Founded
BengaluruBase
Full-stackApproach

At a glance

  • Training and inference infrastructure
  • Frontier-model research
  • Enterprise, developer and government deployment
  • Selected sovereign-model builder for government

Models & modalities

Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B launched in February 2026, trained from scratch with mixture-of-experts architecture.

  • 30B: 32K context window
  • 105B: 128K context window
  • Sarvam 1: 2-billion-parameter model, Oct 2024
  • Sarvam-M: May 2025; critics noted it was fine-tuned from a foreign base model

Also launched text-to-speech, speech-to-text and a document-parsing vision model.

Developer ecosystem

March 2026 startup programme: up to 12 months of API credits, Sarvam language-AI tools and engineering support.

Its full-stack positioning spans infrastructure, research and deployment.

Select a milestone

Series A: $41M led by Lightspeed, with Peak XV Partners and Khosla Ventures.

Funding figures in this brief

Figures vary by source. Primary Series B figure shown; October reporting also cited $255M + $90M.

Build → deploy → monetise

Potential routes to value include API usage, enterprise and government deployments, and developer adoption.

Startup programme

Up to 12 months of API credits, language-AI tools and engineering support may lower experimentation barriers and build developer adoption.

Strengths

  • Indic-language focus
  • Full-stack approach
  • Government and enterprise tailwinds

Risks + open question

  • Global competition
  • Heavy compute cost
  • Funding concentration

Can sovereign models win on quality—not just policy?

02 / Founders’ journey

Build for the
real world.

Two founders, a sovereign-AI thesis, and a bet that India’s AI needs deserve more than imported defaults.

Sarvam founders Dr. Vivek Raghavan and Dr. Pratyush Kumar

Dr. Vivek Raghavan

Co-founder of Sarvam, bringing a vision of building AI capabilities that serve India's unique linguistic, technological and societal needs.

Dr. Pratyush Kumar

Co-founder of Sarvam, focused on developing India's sovereign AI ecosystem through foundational research, infrastructure and real-world applications.

  • Infrastructure can be a moat: training, inference and deployment matter beyond the model.
  • Build around context: language and local needs can differentiate.
  • Distribution matters: enterprise, developer and government routes can enable adoption.
  • Capital intensity is real: compute-heavy businesses need careful economics.
